question: Scenario: I am preparing a Micron earnings briefing. Reconstruct Q4 from the annual and nine-month filings, reconcile it to the earnings release, then test whether the next-quarter guidance meets my stated revenue and gross-margin hurdles. First, use the FY2025 10-K filed October 3, 2025 to retrieve FY2025 and FY2024 revenue and gross profit in USD millions. Calculate FY2025 gross margin and its change from FY2024 in percentage points. Keep the dollar inputs for the next step. Return rev25: number (USD million); gp25: number (USD million); rev24: number (USD million); gp24: number (USD million); gm25: number (percent); gm_change: number (percentage points). Cite the SEC document and precise table/note/exhibit. Reuse prior-stage amounts without intermediate rounding; report percentages/ratios to two decimals and monetary derived amounts to three decimals unless specified.
filing_period: FY2025 annual/Q3/Q4 and FY2026 Q1 guidance as announced 2025-09-23
reasoning: Prior-stage dependencies: none. Hop depth 3: depth 1: read_1 -> depth 2: derive_gm25, derive_gm24 -> depth 3: derive_gm_change. gm25 = gp25 / rev25 * 100; gm24 = gp24 / rev24 * 100; gm_change = gm25 - gm24

Reuse prior-stage amounts without intermediate rounding; report percentages/ratios to two decimals and monetary derived amounts to three decimals unless specified.

question: Finish the briefing using Step 4's lower-bound revenue growth and Step 3's reconciled Q4 gross margin. My briefing rule requires at least 5% sequential revenue growth at the guidance low end AND at least a 3-percentage-point increase in GAAP gross margin at its guidance low end. Retrieve FY2026 Q1 GAAP gross-margin guidance from the same exhibit, compute its lower bound and uplift versus Q4, and return whether both hurdles pass. Do not substitute non-GAAP guidance. Return gm_low: number (percent); uplift: number (percentage points); both_pass: boolean (boolean). Cite the SEC document and precise table/note/exhibit. Reuse prior-stage amounts without intermediate rounding; report percentages/ratios to two decimals and monetary derived amounts to three decimals unless specified.
